questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a motorcyclist?
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing when riding. Good protective gear includes a sturdy jacket that covers your arms and legs, boots or heavy shoes that cover and support your ankles, and sturdy gloves.

questions.question: A motorcycle's brake light is:

options.text: More noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less important than a car's brake lights.
More easily seen than a car's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is usually not as noticeable as a car's brake lights. Flash your brake light before you slow down or stop to help other drivers see that you are braking.

questions.question: When it is obvious that you are going to turn, you:

options.text: Do not need to use a turn signal.
Should still use a turn signal.
Only need to use a turn signal if there are nearby pedestrians.
Only need to use a turn signal if you are at a stop light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should still use a turn signal.
questions.explanation: Always use a turn signal when you turn or change lanes, even if you think your intention is obvious. Use signals all the time. Other vehicles may be nearby that you cannot see.

questions.question: Low-speed crashes:

options.text: Happen frequently, so there is no need to worry about them.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen at speeds below 30 miles per hour. Even low-speed crashes can cause death.

questions.question: The shortest and safest stops happen when you:

options.text: Allow the front tire to lock up.
Use both the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: The shortest and safest stops happen when you use both the front and rear brakes smoothly and gradually, without skidding either tire.

questions.question: For maximum protection, wear a helmet certified by the:
questions.explanation: For maximum protection, use a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards.

questions.question: A good way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make obscene gestures.
Speed up to create distance between you and the tailgater.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate at a higher speed, which increases danger.

questions.question: When choosing a lane position, you should think about:

options.text: Whether other drivers can see you.
How many cars are on the road ahead.
Which lane position will result in a shorter trip.
If you can pass more vehicles in a certain position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: A good lane position offers several benefits. Most importantly, make sure other drivers can see you and you have enough space around your motorcycle.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Assume the passenger has ridden a motorcycle before.
Not assume the passenger has ridden a motorcycle before and explain what to do.
Not explain anything since they are only a passenger, not the operator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the passenger has ridden a motorcycle before and explain what to do.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle passenger needs to understand how to stay safe. Never assume a passenger knows what to do. Give complete instructions before every ride.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should:

options.text: Pick a favorite portion of the lane and stay there all the time.
Continually weave among lane positions to keep other drivers out.
Choose a lane position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best or should always be avoided. Change your lane position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Ride on the shoulder away from other traffic.

questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes, slow down, and avoid sudden movements. Watch for oil, shade, dirt, gravel, and bridges. These surfaces have less grip than normal pavement.

questions.question: What is the danger of riding next to a car?

options.text: You may be in the driver's blind spot.
It is only a problem on wet roads.
It makes driving easier for the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding directly beside another vehicle is dangerous. The driver may not see you in their blind spot. Also, the vehicle blocks your escape route.

questions.question: Which surface is slippery for a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Slippery surfaces include wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, and metal covers in the road. Ride with extra care on these surfaces.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: You do not need to look over your shoulder if you use your mirrors.
Mirrors show everything around your motorcycle.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Assume drivers will respond properly to your signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. Always turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: Why should you keep distance between you and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: To give you time and space to see and react to dangers.
So traffic counters can count you as a vehicle.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: To give you time and space to see and react to dangers.
questions.explanation: Following distance gives you space to stop or swerve if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly. It also helps you see road hazards like potholes.

questions.question: On which surface does a motorcycle have the best grip?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, and metal covers provide poor grip. Dry pavement is safest for motorcyclists.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid an object or uneven surface, what should you do?

options.text: Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Rise off the seat so your legs can absorb the shock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise off the seat so your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Approach the obstacle at a 90-degree angle. Slow down as much as possible. Keep the motorcycle upright. Rise slightly off the seat so your knees absorb impact. Just before hitting it, gently open the throttle to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: What can help prevent crashes?

options.text: Keep your plans hidden from other drivers.
Always stay within a foot of another vehicle.

questions.explanation: Be visible by using your signals, brake light, and lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle. Always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: Before riding, check your tires for all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Before riding, check tire air pressure, tread, and general wear.

questions.question: What does a face shield do?

options.text: Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, impact-resistant face shield gives the best protection for your eyes and face. Eyeglasses are not enough. In Vermont, a windshield can replace a shield, though a shield is still recommended.

questions.question: Which of the following do you NOT need to check before every ride?
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your motorcycle carefully. Look at the rims and spokes for bends, looseness, or damage. Check the tire condition and tread. Check all the lights.

questions.question: How do you control the accelerator on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The accelerator is on the right handgrip. You control it with your right hand.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Which type of sign is rectangular?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, like speed limit signs, are rectangular and white with black lettering or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: What material are motorcycle riding gloves usually made of?
questions.explanation: Motorcycle gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.
